note: The five factions (S3.4 stubs, filled out in S3.5; brief §11). Ids are stable; names are working names until S7.4 settles them (D-012). Each has a `line` (who they are in a sentence), a `look` (how their ships and docks read on Margo's monitor), `values`, what they `buys` and `bans` (goods are words until Stage 7 makes them content), how they treat `smugglers`, the enemy `ships` they fly (content/ships/), and a `voice` note for writers. Nothing reads look, buys, bans or voice in play yet: Stage 7 gives them prices, inspections and patrols (DF-50).

items.name: The Receivers
items.line: What is left of the company's administrators, reclaiming assets one patrol line at a time.
items.look: Company grey with the old crest painted over and painted back. Clean ships, too few of them, every hull number on a list.
items.values: Process, recovery, the idea that the Reach still belongs to someone. They believe the paperwork will save them, and it might.
bans: anything under a broken company seal
items.smugglers: Inspect everyone, fine everything, seize what they can carry. They want the cargo more than the crew.
items.voice: Polite, procedural, tired. Reads from cards. Says 'asset' where anyone else would say 'ship' or 'person'.

items.name: The Outer Stations Union
items.line: The miners' union that keeps the outer stations breathing, and keeps a list.
items.look: Patched yellow hulls, hand-lettered names, ore tenders turned into everything else. Docks that smell of hot metal and soup.
items.values: Shares, safety lines, nobody left behind on a rock. Long memories for who paid and who did not.
items.smugglers: Look the other way for anything that keeps a station running. Turn you over to the Receivers for anything that does not.
items.voice: Blunt, warm until it is not. Calls everyone by a first name. Counts things out loud.

items.name: The Quiet Order
items.line: A religious order that thinks the emptiness of the Reach is holy and should stay that way.
items.look: Ships stripped of every light they can live without, hulls scratched with long lines of small writing. Their docks are dim on purpose.
items.values: Silence, distance, letting the dead lie where they fell. They do not trust anything that hums.
buys: salvage from the old pilgrim ships
bans: ship minds they have not blessed
items.smugglers: Do not search. They ask what you carry, and they remember the answer.
items.voice: Short sentences, long pauses. Never raises a voice. Refers to Margo as 'your machine'.

items.name: The Free Confederation
items.line: Pirate crews with a written code. The code is long, and mostly about shares.
items.look: Mismatched plating, a different flag on every ship, and the same red stripe on all of them. Docks with more guns than cranes.
items.values: The code, the share, and getting paid. A deal kept is sacred; a deal broken is a debt with interest.
buys: anything that fell off a company ship
items.smugglers: Smugglers are customers. Informants are cargo.
items.voice: Cheerful, quick, a lot of numbers. Quotes the code by article. Threats delivered as advice.

items.name: Reach Medical Cooperative
items.line: A medical and research collective that pays well and asks very few questions.
items.look: White hulls kept white at some cost, cold-chain markings, clinics that are cleaner than anything else in the Reach.
items.values: Research, results, and the patients who pay for both. They mean well about as often as anyone does.
bans: unlicensed medicine sold by anyone but them
items.smugglers: Will hire you to smuggle and report you for smuggling, depending on the cargo.
items.voice: Precise, kind in a clinical way. Thanks you for your cooperation before you have given it.
